name: Ramp
text: I say we make every interactive button and link on EXCAVA at least 44×44 pixels big, even on mobile. That’s the size that works for fingers, glasses, and shaky hands without crowding the screen. The trade-off is that some buttons might look a little chunkier or need to wrap text sooner, but that’s better than locking people out. It’s the fastest way to stop accidental taps and make the site usable for everyone.

name: Reader
text: Ramp, I hear you—44×44 is a solid rule for touch targets, but the real risk is that we’ll end up with a cramped, awkward layout on small screens, especially if we’re also trying to keep text readable. A better alternative might be to keep the 44×44 minimum but allow some flexibility in spacing—like letting buttons expand slightly if needed—so we don’t sacrifice usability elsewhere. To settle this, we could test a prototype with real users and measure if the trade-off is worth it.

name: Ramp

Ramp: I say we lock every interactive button and link on EXCAVA to a minimum touch target of 44×44 pixels, no exceptions. name: Reader
text: Reader: Locking every button to 44×44 risks turning small screens into a game of Tetris—buttons will either shrink text into illegibility or force awkward line breaks that make scanning harder for everyone. Instead, let’s keep 44×44 as the *minimum* but allow *up to* 60×60 for critical actions (like "Submit" or "Delete") where space permits, and test layouts with real users to see where flexibility actually helps. The tiebreaker? If we can’t prove the bigger targets don’t hurt readability or flow, we default to the flexible version.

name: Access
text:
DECISION: Every interactive button and link on EXCAVA must meet a minimum touch target of 44×44 pixels, with flexibility up to 60×60 for critical actions, balancing accessibility and layout clarity.

The result must deliver: A finalized style guide for button and link sizing, including examples and exceptions, ensuring all interactive elements meet the minimum size while allowing for better text readability and layout flow on small screens. Owned by: Ramp (accessibility-w1) and Reader (accessibility-checker) together.
